method: Company-stated in-service schedule for contracted MW that is neither online nor already scheduled at Epoch-tracked sites. "2026" = after the retrieval date to year-end. A phase with a start and finish date is placed in its finish year. Grades: A filed, B company-stated (call/deck/PR), C press, D analyst. Power bases follow each company (mostly critical IT; Crusoe and Cipher gross; Nebius connected). Landlord and tenant rows overlap (Fluidstack MW sit in TeraWulf, Hut 8 and Cipher rows; CoreWeave MW in Galaxy, Applied Digital and Core Scientific rows), so rows are not additive.
caveats: Landlord and tenant rows double count each other: Fluidstack MW also sit in TeraWulf, Hut 8 and Cipher rows, and CoreWeave capacity also sits in the Galaxy, Applied Digital and Core Scientific rows. Epoch attributes Helios, Ellendale, Denton, Muskogee, Dalton and Marble to CoreWeave only.

The power basis is mixed: most landlord schedules are critical IT, while Crusoe (gross), Cipher (gross), TensorWave (facility), Nebius (connected) and Epoch (facility) are not. Nothing was rescaled unless the row says so.
Q3 2026 results for CoreWeave (Nov 10), Hut 8 (Nov 4), IREN (Nov 5), TeraWulf (Nov 6), Nebius (Nov 12) and Fermi (~Nov 12) were not yet published as of 2026-11-03.

items.basis: Core Scientific Q2 2026 deck (8-K exhibit), slide 9: CoreWeave at Dalton, GA ~175 MW leased, ~30 MW billing, 'Est. completion early 2027' -> ~145 MW critical IT still to come. Epoch carries Dalton flat at 40 MW, so this is outside the Epoch part.

CoreWeave.overlap_with_epoch: CoreWeave's year-end target is cumulative and fleet-wide, so Epoch's tracked sites are inside it. Of the +350 MW implied for H2 2026, Epoch already shows +124 MW after Nov 3 (Ellendale +26, Muskogee +98), so the 2026 segment is net 226. Additions at Epoch sites between 6/30 and 11/3 are not in online_mw (6/30) and not in Epoch's after-now figure, so they correctly stay inside the 226. Helios (Galaxy) sits entirely in the Epoch part. Galaxy's own schedule is Phase II 260 MW IT with data-hall deliveries beginning Q2 2027 and Phase III 133 MW IT in 2028. That equals CoreWeave 10-Q Q2 2026's '393 MW of electrical power remained undelivered at the site and was expected to be delivered in phases in 2026 and 2028'. Epoch instead shows Helios +400 facility MW in 2028 and +200 in 2029+, about one year later than Galaxy states, so the Epoch Helios timing should arguably shift to 2027 (+~395 facility) and 2028 (+~200). The 10-Q also says '355 MW of electrical power remains undelivered at these sites' (construction-cost-based leases, unnamed, likely Ellendale/Applied Digital) 'between 2026 and 2028'. That is probably also in the Epoch part and is not used here. Epoch figures are facility MW, while CoreWeave 'active power' is undefined in filings (landlord leases feeding it are critical IT). No scaling applied, so the 124 MW subtraction may slightly overstate the overlap.

Reaffirmed in the Q2 2026 release: 'targeted for initial data hall delivery in the second quarter of 2027'.

Beacon Point Phase 1 (Nueces County TX, high-IG tenant, 352 MW IT, six data halls): 'initial energization in the first quarter of 2027 and initial data hall delivery in the third quarter of 2027' (Q2 2026 release). The full-delivery date is not stated. In the June 2026 notes presentation, the revenue waterfall ($63M in 2027, $489M in 2028, $545M in 2029, then ~3% escalators) implies full run-rate is reached during 2028. Hut 8 / Highrise.notes: 949 MW IT = River Bend 245 + Beacon Point Phase 1 352 + Phase 2 352 (Q2 2026 release: '949 MW of contracted IT capacity'). Utility capacity: River Bend 330 MW, Beacon Point ~1,000 MW (500 per phase). The schedule uses IT MW, matching the contracted basis. Sum = 949 = remainder. The Q3 2026 results are due Nov 4, 2026, after this cut-off, so they were not available. The latest filed statements are the Aug 4, 2026 release/10-Q. Under an initial-year convention, Beacon Point P1 would move to 2027, making 2027 597 and 2028 352. Excludes River Bend's 1,000 MW ROFO expansion (not contracted).

VNET.notes: Confirmed in the Q2 2026 6-K ex.99-1 (2026-08-18): 'Capacity in service was 1,007MW', 'Total capacity committed was 970MW', and 'Commitment rate for capacity in service was 96.3%' (wholesale, as of 2026-06-30). The 970 MW is a commitment on capacity already in service, so contracted minus online is negative and the remainder is 0. Separately, 'Capacity under construction was 585MW' (wholesale); the release gives no pre-commitment MW or delivery dates for it, and it is not part of the 970 MW.
